fun_facts: At Saraland High School, Ryan Coleman-Williams was Alabama’s only two-time Mr. Football. In three seasons, he had more than 4,400 yards of total offense and scored 76 touchdowns in 39 games.
He skipped his senior year of high school to join Alabama, and was 17 as a freshman.
As a freshman against Georgia, he caught six passes for 177 yards and a touchdown.
One of his plays against Georgia was a 75-yard touchdown catch featuring a spin move that helped Alabama win.
In 2024, he had 48 catches for 865 yards and eight receiving touchdowns, plus two rushing touchdowns.
In 2026, he recorded 32 catches for 497 yards and four touchdowns, averaging 15.5 yards per catch.

"Somebody texted me and said, 'I bet you're glad Ryan Williams reclassified,'" said Ham Barnett, head coach at St. Paul's Episcopal School in Mobile. "I told him my defensive backs were happy for sure."
